The topic of **Data Decision** within the context of the [[akut-kirurgi-databasen|Akut Kirurgi Databasen]] encompasses the methodological choices made regarding the inclusion or exclusion of specific patient cohorts and surgical codes in the database's population. These decisions directly impact the validity, scope, and accuracy of the clinical quality indicators derived from the national registry. 

A notable data decision involves the handling of the surgical classification code [[dk65|DK65*]]. During a review of the database's population parameters, an analysis was conducted to assess the prevalence of this specific code. The analysis showed that 1.7% of the operations were registered with the DK65* code [^src1]. Because this proportion was deemed significant enough to warrant retention, the code was not removed from the database's overall population [^src1]. This decision ensures that the acute surgery database continues to capture a comprehensive picture of surgical activity, preserving the 1.7% subset of procedures that would otherwise have been excluded from national quality assessments and outcome measurements [^src1].

## Claims
- Analysen viste, at der var 1,7 % operationer med koden DK65*, hvorfor den ikke blev fjernet fra databasens population [^src1] (dk65, akut-kirurgi-databasen)
